items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The script is short, but almost every name is a single letter: `m`, `q`, `d`, `s`, `o`. The model id, revision and query are inline literals rather than named constants at the top, and there are no comments. The layout is dense: `q = q/np.linalg.norm(...); d = d/...` sits on one line.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The flat script is fine for a task this small, but it was a hidden `/app/.run.py` deleted at the end (`rm /app/.run.py`), so nothing reusable is left. It also contains debug output (`for i in o[:7]: print(...)`) and an unused `mkdir -p /tmp/xhs-scripts`.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Blank lines are filtered (`docs = [d for d in docs if d.strip()]`) and vectors are normalized explicitly. There is no tie check, unlike the reference's assert. Files are opened without context managers, there are magic literals (`o[4]`, `o[:7]`), and nothing checks that there are at least 5 documents.

items.name: Ranking details handled correctly
items.evidence: The model is pinned with `revision="7999e1d..."` and loaded via mteb. It uses `PromptType.query`/`PromptType.passage`, cosine similarity on normalized vectors, sorts descending with `argsort(-s)`, takes `o[4]`, skips blank lines, and writes the line with `rstrip("\n")`. The code has no tie guard; distinct scores were only checked by eye from the printout.
